Replace with definitive vascular access (peripheral IV or central line) within 24 hours.

complications: Skin necrosis from prolonged extravasation of vasoactive drugs
postProcedureCare: Document time of insertion clearly; remove within 24 hours
Monitor limb for swelling, redness, perfusion, and pain
Replace with peripheral IV or central line as soon as safe
Post-removal: clean dressing, observe for signs of osteomyelitis at follow-up

references.label: ILCOR 2020 Consensus on Resuscitation (IO access in cardiac arrest)
Tobias JD, Ross AK. Intraosseous infusions. Anesth Analg 2010

title: Intraosseous access — tibial (adult, alternative protocol)
indications: Failed peripheral IV access in emergency.

relative: Recent IO same bone within 48 h.

equipment: EZ-IO driver or manual IO needle.
consentNotes: Explain risks (pain on flush, infection, fracture, compartment syndrome) and consent if conscious.

steps.step: Identify landmark — proximal tibia, 2 finger-breadths below tibial tuberosity, medial flat surface.
Insert IO needle perpendicular to bone surface.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop driver when in marrow space.

steps.step: Remove stylet, confirm placement with aspiration or saline flush.
steps.detail: Aspirate marrow / smooth flush confirms placement.

steps.safetyCheck: Apply pressure bag for adult flow.

steps.step: Local anaesthetic 1 % lidocaine 2 mL slow push before any large bolus in conscious patient.

postProcedureCare: Replace IO with IV access within 24 h.

complications.management: Fasciotomy if confirmed; remove IO immediately.
Antibiotics tailored to organism; debridement if severe.
Lidocaine prior to bolus; reduce flow.

title: Midline catheter insertion
indications: Avoidance of central line where possible.
consentNotes: Explain risks of catheter-related bloodstream infection, thrombosis, mechanical injury, and need for daily review.

steps.step: Position arm and identify basilic / brachial / cephalic vein with US.
steps.detail: Choose vein with adequate depth and diameter.

steps.step: Local anaesthetic to skin and tissues.
Cannulate vein under direct US guidance.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm wire in vein, not artery.

steps.step: Advance catheter to tip at mid-axillary level (no central tip).
Secure catheter and apply transparent dressing.

redFlags: Swelling, pain, erythema at insertion site.
postProcedureCare: Flush with saline before and after each use.
Remove at completion of therapy or if complication.

complications.management: Remove catheter, blood cultures, IV antibiotics.
Local pressure; specialist input if persistent.

references.label: Royal College of Nursing Vascular Access

title: Subclavian central venous catheter — landmark technique
consentNotes: Explain risk of pneumothorax, haemothorax, arterial puncture, infection, and arrhythmia. Document consent or rationale for emergency placement.

steps.step: Position supine head-down 15°, head turned away.
Identify landmarks — junction of medial and middle third of clavicle.
Local anaesthetic to skin and periosteum.
Insert needle below clavicle, advancing horizontally toward sternal notch.
Seldinger technique — wire then dilator then catheter.

references.label: AAGBI / Intensive Care Society Central Line

title: Nasogastric tube insertion — adult
equipment: NG tube of appropriate size (Ryle 14–16 Fr for decompression, fine-bore 8–10 Fr for feeding).
consentNotes: Counsel on discomfort during insertion, gagging, mild bleeding; rare risks of mispositioning or aspiration.

steps.step: Position upright with chin to chest.
Measure tube — nose to ear to xiphisternum.
Pass tube along the floor of nose into pharynx.
Ask patient to swallow water; advance tube during swallowing.
Stop if coughing / cyanosis — withdraw to nasopharynx.
Confirm position by pH < 5.5 of aspirate.
steps.safetyCheck: DO NOT use auscultation alone — discredited.

steps.step: Secure with tape; chest X-ray if pH ambiguous or before feeding.
steps.safetyCheck: Use X-ray gold standard if any doubt.

postProcedureCare: Daily review of site and need.

complications.management: Stop feeding; CT chest; surgical input.

title: Urinary catheterisation — female (adult)
indications: Accurate fluid balance in critical care.
equipment: Saline + 10 mL syringe to inflate balloon.
consentNotes: Explain procedure, risk of catheter-related UTI, urethral trauma, bypassing. Document consent.

steps.step: Position supine with knees flexed and abducted.
Identify urethral meatus between clitoris and vagina.
Insert catheter using sterile no-touch technique.

steps.safetyCheck: Stop if patient experiences sudden pain — possible urethral inflation.

steps.step: Gently pull catheter back until balloon engages at bladder neck.
Connect to drainage bag below bladder level.

complications.management: Remove catheter if possible; antibiotics if symptomatic.

title: Paediatric urinary catheterisation
indications: Urine sample in non-toilet-trained child where in-out catheter recommended.
equipment: Paediatric Foley (size by age — 6Fr infants, 8–10 Fr toddlers).
consentNotes: Counsel parents on need, risks, comfort measures; consent.

steps.step: Use age-appropriate gel and warmed equipment.
Inflate balloon with appropriate volume (3–5 mL infant, 5–10 mL older).
Secure tubing to thigh with appropriate dressing.

complications.management: Antibiotics if symptomatic; review for removal.
Paediatric urology input; suprapubic if needed.

title: Suprapubic catheter insertion (revision technique)
indications: Urethral stricture not amenable to dilation.

relative: Lower midline scar suggesting bowel adhesion.

consentNotes: Counsel on risk of bowel injury, bleeding, infection, blockage. Consent.

steps.step: Confirm bladder full (≥ 300 mL on US).
Sterile preparation midline 2 finger-breadths above pubic symphysis.
Local anaesthetic to skin and tissues, including 'sound' for bladder.
Insert trocar perpendicular to skin, aiming at coccyx.
Withdraw trocar leaving catheter in place; inflate balloon.

title: Radial arterial line insertion — ultrasound-guided
indications: Continuous BP monitoring in shock / vasopressor use.

relative: Recent radial artery cannulation same site.

consentNotes: Explain risk of arterial spasm, thrombosis, infection, distal ischaemia. Consent.

steps.step: Confirm collateral with Allen test or ultrasound.
Identify radial artery on ultrasound; cannulate using direct visualisation.
Connect to transducer system; zero at phlebostatic axis.

complications.management: Remove cannula; cultures; antibiotics if systemic.

title: Ultrasound-guided peripheral IV cannulation
consentNotes: Explain procedure and risks (failure, haematoma).

steps.step: Sterile cover for probe + clean skin with chlorhexidine.
Identify vein in short or long axis view.
Insert cannula at 30–45° angle under direct visualisation of needle tip.
Confirm flashback then advance cannula off needle.

complications.management: Escalate to senior or alternative access.

title: Large-volume therapeutic paracentesis (≥ 5 L)
equipment: Pleural drainage kit or pigtail catheter.
consentNotes: Counsel on risks of bleeding, infection, hypotension; benefits of symptom relief and reduced HRS risk with albumin.

steps.step: US-mark site avoiding inferior epigastric and bowel.
steps.detail: Avoid LIF/RIF in pregnancy or large bowel.

steps.step: Local anaesthetic to skin and tissues.
Insert pigtail catheter with Seldinger technique.
Drain freely; do not clamp / limit volume.
steps.detail: Continue until bag empty or symptoms relieved.

steps.step: Administer 8 g albumin per L drained > 5 L.
Remove catheter once drainage complete; cover puncture site.

postProcedureCare: Review need for diuretic and dietary advice.

title: Knee joint aspiration and corticosteroid injection

absolute: Septic arthritis suspected (do diagnostic aspiration only, not steroid).

consentNotes: Explain risk of bleeding, infection, post-injection flare, fat atrophy/depigmentation.

steps.step: Position patient supine, knee slightly flexed.
Insert needle under patella into joint space.
Aspirate fluid; send for cell count + culture + crystals.
If injecting steroid, replace syringe (not needle) and inject.

title: Shoulder joint aspiration and injection
indications: Steroid injection for adhesive capsulitis / OA / inflammatory arthritis.
consentNotes: Counsel on risks: infection, bleeding, post-injection flare, tendon damage.

steps.step: Position patient seated with arm relaxed at side.
Identify posterior approach 2 cm inferior and 1 cm medial to posterolateral acromion.
Insert needle aimed toward coracoid; aspirate then inject.

title: Abscess incision and drainage — large / complex

absolute: Anatomical site requiring specialist input (perianal / vulval / breast).

consentNotes: Counsel on procedure, scarring, recurrence, need for packing follow-up.

steps.step: Local anaesthetic infiltration around abscess (not centrally).
steps.safetyCheck: Note that infected tissue blunts local anaesthetic effect.

steps.step: Make linear incision over fluctuant point.
Express purulent contents and break loculations with finger or forceps.
Pack with absorbent ribbon (not too tight).

postProcedureCare: Daily dressing change with packing reduction.

title: Needle cricothyroidotomy — emergency airway
equipment: Jet ventilation system or 3-way tap + oxygen tubing.
consentNotes: Emergency procedure — implied consent.

steps.step: Identify cricothyroid membrane below thyroid cartilage.
Insert 14 G cannula caudally at 45° angle.
Advance cannula off needle; remove needle.
Connect to jet ventilation system or oxygen via 3-way tap.
steps.detail: Adequate oxygenation while definitive airway sought.

steps.step: Plan transition to definitive airway / surgical airway.

postProcedureCare: Convert to definitive airway / surgical airway within 30–45 min.

title: Paediatric bag-mask ventilation

relative: Severe craniofacial abnormality requiring specialist airway.

consentNotes: Emergency procedure.

steps.step: Position head in neutral sniffing position (child) or neutral (infant).
Choose correctly sized mask (covers mouth + nose, not eyes / chin).
Two-handed E-C technique or two-person ventilation if needed.
Squeeze bag at 1 breath every 3–5 sec (paediatric) or 1 every 6 sec (post-ROSC).
Adjust force to produce visible chest rise only.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if no chest rise — reassess airway.
Plan definitive airway if persistent need.

postProcedureCare: Transition to definitive airway as needed.
Document tidal volumes and any difficulty.

title: Supraglottic airway (i-gel) insertion
indications: Elective short anaesthetic where ETT not required.
equipment: i-gel of correct size for body weight.
consentNotes: Counsel re sore throat, dental injury, displacement; implied consent in emergency.

steps.step: Choose i-gel size by weight (4 for 50–90 kg adults).
Lubricate the back, sides, and front of cuff.
Insert i-gel along hard palate then through pharynx until resistance felt.
Confirm placement with chest rise, capnography, auscultation.
Secure with tape; ventilate with BVM.

title: Paediatric endotracheal intubation

relative: Difficult airway anticipated — call senior anaesthetist.

equipment: Cuffed or uncuffed ETT correct size for age.
consentNotes: Emergency or planned with parental consent where time permits.

steps.step: Calculate ETT size by age: cuffed = (age/4) + 3.5; uncuffed = (age/4) + 4.
Use sniffing position with shoulder roll in infants.
Pass ETT under direct vision; advance until depth markers.
Confirm position with capnography + chest rise + auscultation.

complications.management: Stop attempt + ventilate + atropine if needed.

title: Video laryngoscopy — adult

relative: Severe maxillofacial trauma may require surgical airway.

equipment: Video laryngoscope (e.g. GlideScope, Storz CMAC, McGrath).
consentNotes: Emergency or implied consent; explain in non-emergent.

steps.step: Open mouth and insert blade midline.
Advance until glottis visible on screen.
Pass ETT under indirect view using stylet.

postProcedureCare: Document the technique, view (Cormack-Lehane), and any difficulty.
Alert future operators if difficult airway.

complications.management: Switch technique; surgical airway if needed.

title: Bougie-aided tracheal intubation
indications: Difficult intubation with limited glottic view.
consentNotes: Emergency or implied consent.

steps.step: Achieve best laryngeal view with laryngoscope.
Pass bougie beneath the epiglottis aiming midline.
Confirm bougie in trachea by clicks or distal hold-up at 30–35 cm.
Railroad ETT over bougie with laryngoscope still in mouth.
steps.safetyCheck: Rotate tube 90° anticlockwise if catches at arytenoid.

steps.step: Remove bougie; confirm placement with capnography.

title: Focused cardiac ultrasound (FoCUS / FATE)

absolute: Operator inexperience — refer for formal echo.
relative: Significant cardiac history requiring comprehensive assessment.

equipment: Bedside ultrasound with phased array probe.
consentNotes: Explain procedure as diagnostic aid; consent.

steps.detail: Pericardial effusion + IVC for volume status.

complications.management: Use as adjunct to clinical assessment; obtain formal echo where uncertain.

title: Lung ultrasound — BLUE protocol
indications: Distinguishing cardiogenic vs ARDS vs pneumothorax vs PE.
equipment: Bedside ultrasound with linear (high frequency) or curvilinear probe.
consentNotes: Diagnostic adjunct.

steps.step: Posterior PLAPS point for effusion / consolidation.
Document findings and integrate with clinical.

complications.management: Use with clinical context; CT if needed.

title: Extended FAST (eFAST) ultrasound
consentNotes: Diagnostic adjunct in trauma; implied consent in emergency.
postProcedureCare: Repeat in unstable patient with negative initial.
Surgical / critical care referral if positive.

complications.management: Serial assessment; CT if clinically indicated.

title: Fascia iliaca compartment block — ultrasound-guided
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary weakness, sensory loss, infection risk; consent.

steps.step: Identify femoral artery + iliopsoas under US.
Insert needle in plane to needle tip.
Hydrodissect with saline to confirm position below fascia iliaca.
Inject local anaesthetic in fascial plane after negative aspiration.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if pressure builds — wrong plane.

title: Transversus abdominis plane (TAP) block
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary numbness, bleeding, infection.

steps.step: Identify three muscle layers (external oblique, internal oblique, transversus abdominis) lateral to umbilicus.
Insert needle in plane between IO and TA muscles.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if loss of resistance — reassess.

steps.step: Aspirate before injecting; deposit local anaesthetic.

title: Femoral nerve block — ultrasound-guided
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary motor weakness — falls risk; consent.

steps.step: Position supine, leg extended slightly externally rotated.
Identify femoral artery + nerve lateral to artery on US.
Insert needle in plane lateral to medial.
Aspirate; deposit local anaesthetic around nerve.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm not in nerve — pain on injection = STOP.

steps.step: Document block and motor function pre/post.

title: Emergency pericardiocentesis (echo-guided)

absolute: Aortic dissection causing tamponade — surgical drainage preferred.

consentNotes: Emergency — implied consent.

steps.step: Local anaesthetic to skin and subcutaneous.
Insert needle aiming at left shoulder under US guidance.
Aspirate fluid; confirm with bedside echo with agitated saline injection.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if blood return + arrhythmia — possibly intracardiac.

steps.step: Place pigtail catheter using Seldinger technique.
Document procedure + send fluid for analysis.

title: Chest drain insertion — Seldinger (small-bore)

relative: Severe contralateral disease (single lung at risk).

consentNotes: Counsel on risks of bleeding, infection, pneumothorax (if effusion), organ injury; consent.

steps.step: Mark site with US — usually 'safe triangle' or below effusion.
Local anaesthetic to skin, periosteum, parietal pleura.
Pass guide wire then dilator then small-bore catheter.

complications.management: Limit initial drainage; CPAP / NIV if develops.

title: Adult Advanced Life Support — cardiac arrest
consentNotes: Implied consent in emergency.

steps.step: Confirm cardiac arrest — unresponsive + not breathing.
Start chest compressions 100–120/min at depth 5–6 cm.
Attach defibrillator; analyse rhythm every 2 min.
Shock VF/pulseless VT immediately (150–360 J biphasic).
Adrenaline 1 mg IV/IO every 3–5 min from 2nd cycle in non-shockable / after 3rd shock in shockable.
Amiodarone 300 mg after 3rd shock in VF/pVT.
Continue CPR + assess for ROSC at every rhythm check.

complications.management: Recognise and stop per team consensus.

title: Paediatric Advanced Life Support
consentNotes: Implied consent in emergency.

steps.safetyCheck: Confirm absence of pulse / signs of life.

steps.step: Begin CPR with paediatric ratio 15:2 (lay 30:2) for two rescuers.
Amiodarone 5 mg/kg after 3rd shock for refractory VF.
Identify reversible causes (Hs and Ts including ECMO if available)

title: Neonatal resuscitation — Helping Babies Breathe
indications: Newborn not breathing / inadequate breathing at birth.

absolute: Confirmed lethal congenital anomaly with do-not-resuscitate decision.
relative: Very preterm without consensus — multidisciplinary discussion.

consentNotes: Implied consent.

steps.step: Dry, warm, stimulate, suction if needed.
If not breathing — begin bag-mask ventilation at 40–60/min.
steps.detail: Effective ventilation is the key step.

steps.step: Reassess at 30 sec; if HR < 60 — start chest compressions 3:1.
Continue resuscitation; consider IV adrenaline 10 µg/kg if HR remains < 60.
Post-resuscitation: warming, glucose, oxygen titration, transfer to NICU.
steps.safetyCheck: Cooling for term HIE per criteria.

redFlags: No improvement at 10 min despite resuscitation.

complications.management: Withdrawal in consultation with family + neonatologist.

title: Synchronised electrical cardioversion (elective + emergency)
indications: Atrial fibrillation / flutter with haemodynamic compromise.

relative: Coagulation status not optimised in chronic AF.

consentNotes: Counsel on risk of post-shock arrhythmia, embolism, skin burn, dental injury.

steps.step: Confirm anticoagulation status in AF (TOE if uncertain).
Confirm synchronisation marker on R wave.
Charge and deliver shock at appropriate energy (50–200 J biphasic).
Reassess rhythm post-shock; repeat if needed.

title: Temporary transvenous pacing
indications: Symptomatic bradyarrhythmia not responsive to atropine.
Complete heart block prior to permanent pacing.
consentNotes: Counsel on risks of perforation, arrhythmia, infection.

steps.step: Obtain central venous access (internal jugular or subclavian).
Insert pacing wire under fluoroscopy or ECG guidance.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if perforation suspected — sudden bradycardia.

steps.step: Connect to pacing box; capture at minimum threshold.
Set rate per patient (60–80 bpm typically).

title: Post-cardiac arrest care bundle
indications: Return of spontaneous circulation after cardiac arrest.
consentNotes: Family communication and consent for ongoing care.

steps.step: Coronary angiography in suspected ACS-related arrest.

title: Ultrasound-guided thoracentesis
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection, pneumothorax, organ injury; consent.

steps.step: Identify effusion + safe site with US.
Position patient leaning forward over a table.
Local anaesthetic to skin and pleura.
Insert thoracentesis catheter at marked site.
Aspirate gently; limit to 1.5 L per session to reduce re-expansion oedema.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if persistent cough / chest pain.

title: Ultrasound-guided paracentesis (diagnostic)
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection; consent.

steps.step: Identify safe site with US (avoid inferior epigastric, bowel).
Insert needle perpendicular to skin in marked site.

steps.detail: Send for cell count, culture, biochemistry, cytology.

title: Interscalene brachial plexus block — US-guided
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary phrenic palsy, Horner's syndrome, LAST risk; consent.

steps.step: Position patient supine with head turned away.
Identify brachial plexus between anterior and middle scalene muscles.
Insert needle in plane lateral to medial.
Deposit local anaesthetic around nerve roots after negative aspiration.

title: Supraclavicular brachial plexus block
consentNotes: Counsel on pneumothorax risk, temporary motor weakness, LAST.

steps.step: Position patient supine + head turned away.
Identify subclavian artery + brachial plexus 'cluster of grapes' above clavicle.
Insert needle in plane lateral to medial.
Deposit LA in fascial planes around plexus after negative aspiration.

title: Popliteal sciatic nerve block — US-guided
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary motor weakness, LAST risk; consent.

steps.step: Position patient prone or supine with leg elevated.
Identify sciatic nerve in popliteal fossa, lateral to popliteal artery, before bifurcation.
Insert needle in plane lateral to medial.

title: Erector spinae plane block
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary numbness, LAST.

steps.step: Identify transverse process at desired level.
steps.detail: T5 for thoracic, T7 for abdominal.

steps.step: Insert needle in plane until contacts transverse process.
Deposit LA beneath erector spinae muscle on transverse process.

title: Bedside abdominal aorta ultrasound for AAA
indications: Suspected ruptured AAA in shocked patient.
consentNotes: Diagnostic adjunct.

steps.step: Scan from xiphisternum to umbilicus identifying aorta.

title: Simple interrupted suturing — full technique
indications: Simple linear laceration with clean edges.

absolute: Highly contaminated wounds (open dressing or delayed closure).

consentNotes: Counsel on scarring, infection, suture removal time.

steps.step: Place sutures 2-3 mm from wound edge.

postProcedureCare: Suture removal: face 5 days, scalp 7-10, body 7-10, limbs 10-14.

title: Vertical mattress suture
consentNotes: Standard wound consent.

steps.step: Pass needle deeply through one side of wound (far-far).
Tie knot on the side away from wound.

complications.management: Refer to plastic surgery if face.

title: Subcuticular continuous suture
consentNotes: Standard consent.

steps.step: Confirm wound clean + closed in deep layers.
Begin at one end with anchor stitch.
Pass needle horizontally through dermis from side to side, advancing along wound.
End with anchor stitch + cut suture.

title: Surgical skin staple closure

absolute: Facial / cosmetic wounds (use sutures or adhesive).

consentNotes: Counsel on cosmetic outcome, infection, removal.

steps.step: Press stapler perpendicular to skin, 1 cm spacing.

postProcedureCare: Staple removal: scalp 7-10 days, body 10-14 days.

title: Tissue adhesive (Dermabond)
consentNotes: Counsel on cosmetic outcome, peel-off duration, water exposure.

steps.step: Apply thin layer of adhesive across wound + slightly beyond.

title: Bedside wound debridement
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary worsening of appearance, bleeding, pain.

steps.step: Sharp debridement of clearly necrotic tissue.
Apply appropriate dressing (e.g. hydrocolloid for granulation).

title: Foreign body removal from skin
indications: Embedded foreign body in superficial tissue (glass, wood, metal).
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection, residual material, scarring.

steps.step: Small incision over FB if needed.

steps.detail: Take time to identify all fragments.

steps.step: Close wound (suture, adhesive, or open dressing).

title: Subungual haematoma trephination
equipment: Sterile cautery / heated paperclip / 18 G needle.
consentNotes: Counsel on cosmetic outcome, infection, drainage.

steps.step: Insert heated cautery / paperclip / needle gently through nail plate.

title: Partial toenail avulsion for ingrown nail
consentNotes: Counsel on cosmetic change, recurrence, infection.

steps.step: Apply tourniquet at base of toe.
Elevate nail margin from nail bed.
Phenolisation of matrix to prevent regrowth.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm protection of normal nail bed.

title: Burn dressing application
consentNotes: Counsel on pain during dressing change, cosmetic outcome, follow-up.

steps.step: Apply silver dressing or hydrocolloid per wound stage.
Document and plan next dressing change.

title: Short-arm cast application

relative: Severe soft tissue swelling (use backslab first).

consentNotes: Counsel on cast care, signs of compartment syndrome, removal date.

steps.step: Apply cast padding 2-3 layers, more at bony prominences.
Apply plaster / fibreglass material in spiral.

complications.management: Remove cast urgently; fasciotomy if confirmed.

title: Long-leg cast application
consentNotes: Counsel on cast care, weight-bearing status, removal date.

title: Upper GI endoscopy — diagnostic
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure, sedation risks, perforation (rare), aspiration, sore throat, missed lesion.

steps.step: Pass scope through oesophagus to duodenum.

title: Variceal band ligation

relative: Gastric / fundic varices (use glue / TIPS instead).

consentNotes: Counsel on rebleeding risk, dysphagia, perforation, sedation.

steps.step: Suction varix into banding device cap.

postProcedureCare: Repeat banding every 2-4 weeks until obliteration.

title: Colonoscopy with polypectomy
consentNotes: Counsel on bowel preparation, sedation, perforation (1:1000), bleeding (5 %), missed lesion.

steps.step: Bowel preparation completed; clear fluid only the day before.
Pass scope through entire colon to terminal ileum.
Polypectomy with snare ± clipping for haemostasis.
steps.detail: Cold snare for diminutive / hot snare for larger.

title: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)

absolute: Asymptomatic stones in low-risk patient (alternative imaging).

consentNotes: Counsel on pancreatitis (5–10 %), bleeding, perforation, infection.

steps.step: Cannulate ampulla of Vater under fluoroscopy.
Rectal indomethacin to prevent post-ERCP pancreatitis.

title: Flexible bronchoscopy — diagnostic + therapeutic
consentNotes: Counsel on cough, bleeding, hypoxia, pneumothorax.

steps.step: Pass scope through nose / mouth into trachea.
Take biopsy / BAL / brush as required.

postProcedureCare: Chest X-ray if biopsied / suspected pneumothorax.

title: Spontaneous vaginal delivery — standard
indications: Uncomplicated singleton cephalic pregnancy at term in established labour.
consentNotes: Birth plan discussion; informed consent.

steps.step: Continuous CTG / intermittent auscultation per risk.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop if Category 3 trace — expedite delivery.
Stop and call for help if shoulder dystocia.

steps.step: Place baby on mother's chest; delayed cord clamping 1-3 min.
Active management of third stage with syntometrine / oxytocin.
Examine for tears; repair as needed.

title: Forceps-assisted vaginal delivery
consentNotes: Counsel on indications + risks + alternative (caesarean / ventouse); informed consent.

steps.step: Confirm prerequisites — fully dilated + head engaged + station ≥ +2.
Traction with contraction along J-shaped curve.
steps.safetyCheck: Stop after 3 contractions if no descent.

title: Vacuum (ventouse) assisted vaginal delivery
consentNotes: Counsel on benefits, risks of failure or trauma, neonatal cephalohaematoma; consent.

steps.step: Confirm prerequisites — fully dilated + engaged head.
Traction during contractions, coordinated with maternal pushing.

title: Emergency caesarean section
consentNotes: Time-critical consent for benefits + risks (haemorrhage, infection, organ injury, anaesthetic risk, fetal scalpel injury).

steps.detail: Time targets: Cat I within 30 min.

steps.step: Anaesthetic technique per urgency (Cat I usually GA, Cat II/III regional).
Pfannenstiel skin incision; deepen to uterus.

title: Closed reduction of Colles' fracture
indications: Distal radius fracture with significant dorsal angulation > 10° or shortening.
equipment: Manipulation under appropriate anaesthesia (haematoma / regional block).
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + cast care + need for follow-up + risk of re-displacement.

steps.step: Adequate anaesthesia (haematoma block / Bier block / sedation).
Position patient supine with arm abducted.
Manipulate fracture with palmar pressure on distal fragment.
Apply backslab cast in neutral position.

postProcedureCare: X-ray at 1 week to check position.

title: Anterior shoulder dislocation reduction

absolute: Open injury / fracture-dislocation requiring open reduction.

consentNotes: Counsel on sedation + procedure + recurrence risk.

steps.step: Adequate analgesia + sedation (e.g. procedural sedation, intra-articular lignocaine).
Choose reduction technique (Kocher / Cunningham / Stimson / scapular manipulation).
Apply traction + slow gentle external rotation.
Reduce shoulder with controlled internal rotation.
steps.safetyCheck: Confirm reduction by palpation + smooth motion.

steps.step: Confirm with post-reduction X-ray + neurovascular check.

redFlags: Inability to reduce + need for theatre.
postProcedureCare: Discuss surgical stabilisation in young / recurrent.

title: Hip dislocation reduction
indications: Acute traumatic posterior hip dislocation (most common).
consentNotes: Time-critical procedure (< 6 h reduces AVN risk); informed consent.

steps.step: Confirm with X-ray + CT (femoral head and acetabulum).
Apply traction with knee flexed 90° (Allis method).
Internally / externally rotate to disengage from rim.
Confirm reduction by clinical exam + post-reduction X-ray.
Skin / skeletal traction or hip spica for stable reduction.

title: Ankle fracture-dislocation closed reduction
consentNotes: Time-critical to relieve skin tension; informed consent.

steps.step: Adequate sedation + analgesia (procedural sedation in resus).
Position supine, knee flexed to relax gastrocnemius.
Apply traction along long axis + manipulate foot under direct visualisation.
Apply U-shaped slab + backslab in plantigrade neutral position.

title: Patellar relocation (lateral dislocation)
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + recurrence risk + need for surgical stabilisation.

steps.step: Confirm with X-ray + post-reduction MRI if osteochondral lesion suspected.
Position patient supine with hip slightly flexed.
Extend knee while applying medial pressure to patella.

title: Digital nerve block — finger / toe
equipment: Lignocaine 1 % (no adrenaline historically; 2024 — adrenaline acceptable per evidence).
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary numbness, persistent paraesthesia (rare).

steps.step: Insert needle on each side of base of finger.

postProcedureCare: Avoid heat sources until sensation returns.

title: Local anaesthetic infiltration
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary numbness, allergic reaction (rare), LAST.

steps.step: Confirm allergy status + max safe dose.
Inject slowly while advancing or withdrawing.
Repeat as needed to cover area.

postProcedureCare: Monitor for delayed LAST in larger volumes.

title: Procedural sedation — moderate (conscious)
equipment: Sedation drugs (midazolam + fentanyl, or ketamine, or propofol).
consentNotes: Counsel on sedation depth, recall, respiratory depression, paradoxical reaction.

steps.safetyCheck: Stop and bag-mask if hypoxic / apnoeic.

title: Blood transfusion administration
indications: Symptomatic anaemia (Hb < 70 g/L or 80 g/L if cardiac).
consentNotes: Counsel on alternative options, transfusion reaction risks, infection (rare).

steps.step: Verify patient identification + bedside check with 2 staff.
Establish IV access with large-bore cannula.
Take baseline observations (HR, BP, temp, SpO₂).
Observe at 15 min, then per protocol.

redFlags: Acute haemolytic transfusion reaction (fever, chest pain, dark urine).

title: Bone marrow aspirate and trephine biopsy
consentNotes: Counsel on pain, bleeding, infection.

steps.step: Aspirate 1-2 mL for cytology + cytogenetics + flow cytometry.

title: Percutaneous liver biopsy
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection, biliary leak; consent.

steps.step: Position patient supine; arm above head.

title: Percutaneous renal biopsy
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection, AV fistula; consent.

steps.step: Position patient prone with pillow under abdomen.

title: Intrauterine device (IUD / IUS) insertion
equipment: Sterile speculum + forceps + uterine sound + tenaculum.
consentNotes: Counsel on insertion, pain, expulsion, perforation (1:1000), infection, hormonal effects.

steps.step: Bimanual examination to assess uterus size + position.
Tenaculum on anterior cervix; sound uterus.

title: Pipelle endometrial biopsy
consentNotes: Counsel on cramping, light bleeding post-procedure.

steps.step: Withdraw piston while moving sheath in / out.
Remove pipelle; expel sample into container.

title: Large loop excision of transformation zone (LLETZ / LEEP)
consentNotes: Counsel on bleeding, infection, premature delivery risk in future pregnancy.

steps.step: Pass loop electrode through lesion + transformation zone.
Achieve haemostasis with ball electrode + Monsel's solution.

postProcedureCare: Future antenatal vigilance for cervical incompetence.

title: Inferior alveolar nerve block
indications: Lower jaw analgesia for dental extraction.
consentNotes: Counsel on temporary numbness lip / chin / tongue.

steps.step: Position patient with mouth open wide.
Insert needle parallel to occlusal plane, advance to ramus.

postProcedureCare: Avoid biting / hot drinks until sensation returns.

title: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis administration
indications: Suspected rabies exposure (bite / mucosal / scratch from suspected rabid mammal).

absolute: Confirmed full prior rabies vaccination + recent boost.
relative: Severe allergy to vaccine component (use alternative product).

consentNotes: Counsel on wound care + vaccine schedule + risk if untreated.

steps.step: Immediate wound care: soap + water 15 min + povidone-iodine.
Assess WHO Category I, II, III.
Administer rabies vaccine IM days 0, 3, 7, 14 (28 in immunocompromised).
Administer HRIG / ERIG infiltrated around wound + remainder IM (different site from vaccine) for Category III.

title: Intramuscular injection technique
indications: IM medication (e.g. adrenaline anaphylaxis, antipsychotic, contraceptive).
consentNotes: Confirm consent (or implied in emergency).

steps.step: Confirm patient identity + medication + dose + route + expiry.
Choose site (deltoid for vaccines, vastus lateralis in infants, ventrogluteal preferred for larger volumes).
Clean skin with alcohol; allow to dry.
Stretch skin between fingers (Z-track for irritant medications).
Document site, drug, dose, lot number.

postProcedureCare: Observation per medication (e.g. 15 min after vaccine).

title: Subcutaneous injection technique
consentNotes: Standard consent.

steps.step: Pinch skin; insert needle at 45° (or 90° per device).

title: Oxygen therapy administration
indications: Acute illness with risk of hypoxia.
equipment: Delivery device (nasal cannula, simple mask, non-rebreather, Venturi).
consentNotes: Counsel re fire risk + smoking; confirm target.

steps.step: Choose delivery device based on FiO₂ requirement.
Reassess SpO₂ at 5 min then per protocol.

postProcedureCare: Recheck blood gases if Type 2 risk.

title: Nebuliser administration
consentNotes: Counsel on tremor, palpitations.

steps.step: Choose oxygen-driven (asthma) or air-driven (COPD with Type 2 RF).
Start flow at 6-8 L/min until chamber empty.

complications.management: Switch to air-driven; NIV if rising.
Reduce frequency; consider ICU if severe.

title: Peak expiratory flow measurement

absolute: Severely unwell patient unable to perform manoeuvre.

consentNotes: Counsel + demonstrate technique.

steps.step: Blow out as hard and fast as possible.
Compare to personal best or predicted.

title: 12-lead ECG recording
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure (painless); consent.

steps.step: Apply limb leads (RA, LA, RL, LL).
Document + show to senior immediately if abnormal.

title: Urine dipstick analysis
consentNotes: Standard consent (often implicit).

steps.step: Provide clean container + instructions for midstream sample.
Remove and tap excess on paper towel.
Wait specified time for each square.
Read against chart in good light.
Send for MC&S if positive nitrites / leucocytes / blood / proteinuria.

title: Capillary blood glucose monitoring

relative: Peripheral vascular disease (use ear lobe / alternative site).

consentNotes: Standard consent.

title: Digital rectal examination (PR)
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + discomfort + need for chaperone; consent.

steps.step: Position left lateral with knees to chest.
Assess tone + masses + tenderness + prostate (in men).
Note stool colour on glove (blood, melaena).

complications.complication: Failed examination due to pain / spasm

title: Speculum examination of cervix

absolute: Placenta praevia (DO NOT do digital VE; speculum cautious).

consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + chaperone + samples; consent.

steps.step: Position lithotomy with bottom at edge of bed.
Insert speculum with lubricant at 45° initially.
Inspect cervix + take samples as needed (cytology, swabs).

title: Ankle-brachial pressure index measurement
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + chaperone.

steps.step: Measure brachial systolic BP both arms.
Apply ankle cuff + identify dorsalis pedis or posterior tibial with Doppler.
Inflate cuff to obliterate signal + slowly deflate.
Repeat for both legs at DP + PT.

title: Compression bandaging for venous leg ulcer
equipment: Multi-layer compression bandage system (four-layer or short-stretch).
consentNotes: Counsel on duration of compression + signs to remove + frequency of dressing.

steps.step: Apply padding layer from base of toes to knee.
Apply compression layers per manufacturer instructions.

postProcedureCare: Education on leg elevation + skin care.

title: Clinical breast examination
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + chaperone; consent.

steps.step: Inspect breasts in different positions (sitting, arms raised).
Palpate systematically with flat fingers in concentric circles.
Palpate areola + express to look for discharge.

postProcedureCare: Refer to breast clinic per 2-week wait pathway.

title: Paediatric digital rectal examination
consentNotes: Counsel parent + child about procedure + chaperone; consent.

steps.step: Explain to child + family in age-appropriate terms.
Position young child on parent's lap or left lateral.
Apply generous lubricant + gentle insertion of small finger.
Assess tone, masses, blood on glove.

complications.management: Stop; reschedule under sedation if essential.

title: Paediatric IV cannulation
consentNotes: Counsel parent + child; consent.

steps.step: Apply topical anaesthetic 30-60 min before procedure if time allows.
Identify suitable vein (dorsum hand, antecubital, foot in infants).

complications.management: Escalate to senior or use IO.

title: Nasal foreign body removal
indications: Foreign body in nasal cavity (often paediatric).

absolute: Posterior FB risk of aspiration (specialist removal).

consentNotes: Counsel child + parent; consent.

steps.step: Position child sitting upright, head supported.
Confirm location of FB with nasal speculum + headlight.
Choose technique (forceps, suction, mother's kiss for infants).
Apply topical decongestant if anatomy allows.
Examine both nostrils + ears for other FBs.

redFlags: Suspected button battery / magnet — urgent removal.
postProcedureCare: Plan ENT review if not removed.

title: Aural foreign body removal
indications: Foreign body in external auditory canal (often paediatric).
equipment: Syringe + water for irrigation (non-organic FB only).
consentNotes: Counsel + consent.

steps.step: Determine technique: forceps for solid; irrigation only if non-organic + intact TM.
Position patient and use age-appropriate restraint.

title: Ear syringing / irrigation for wax
indications: Cerumen impaction with hearing loss or fullness.
consentNotes: Counsel on dizziness, bleeding, perforation, infection.

steps.step: Use wax-softening drops (olive oil / sodium bicarbonate) 3-7 days prior.
Position patient with basin under ear.
Direct stream of warmed water (37 °C) at canal roof (not TM).
Inspect canal + TM after each pass.

title: Paediatric temperature measurement
consentNotes: Standard consent.

steps.step: Choose method by age (axillary in infants, tympanic > 4 weeks).

title: Anti-D immunoglobulin administration
indications: Rh-negative pregnant woman with sensitising event (delivery, miscarriage, ECV, abdominal trauma, antenatal bleed).
equipment: Anti-D immunoglobulin (250-500 IU per dose, more for term).
consentNotes: Counsel on rationale, blood product nature, infection risk (very low), consent.

steps.step: Confirm Rh-negative status + Kleihauer test if relevant.
Calculate dose based on sensitising event.
Document dose, batch, expiry, site, date.
Plan repeat at 28 weeks if antenatal.

redFlags: Need for higher dose (large fetomaternal haemorrhage).

title: Activating massive transfusion protocol
indications: Active major haemorrhage (trauma, GI, obstetric, surgical).
Anticipated need for ≥ 4 units RBC in 1 h.
equipment: MTP pack (RBC, FFP, platelets in 1:1:1 ratio).
consentNotes: Time-critical; consent or implied.

steps.step: Send urgent crossmatch + bloods + coagulation + lactate.
Administer O-negative or type-specific blood if delay.
Use 1:1:1 ratio of RBC : FFP : platelets.
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV within 3 h.

title: Airway suctioning — oropharyngeal and tracheal
consentNotes: Standard or emergency.

steps.step: Apply gloves; use sterile technique for tracheal.

title: Cervical collar application
consentNotes: Time-critical; implied consent.

steps.step: Add sand bags / blocks + tape forehead to board.

title: Paediatric safeguarding disclosure interview and documentation
consentNotes: Open conversation with age-appropriate language; explain limits of confidentiality.

steps.step: Explain you will need to tell other people to help keep them safe.
Inform safeguarding lead + social services immediately.
Ensure child is safe before discharge.

complications.management: Specialist sexual / forensic exam if needed.

title: Mental capacity assessment for adult safeguarding
indications: Decision-making capacity unclear (consent to treatment / discharge planning / advance care).

absolute: Patient unable to engage at all.

consentNotes: Counsel patient on purpose; document.

steps.step: Ask patient to demonstrate: understand, retain, weigh up, communicate decision.
If lacks capacity, make best-interest decision.

title: Discussion of resuscitation status (DNACPR)
indications: Patient at risk of cardiac arrest where CPR may be ineffective or contrary to wishes.

relative: Acute distress that may compromise discussion (defer if possible).

consentNotes: Sensitive open conversation; involve family if patient wishes.

steps.step: Explore patient understanding of condition + prognosis.
Explain rationale for discussion + clinical recommendation.
Ask about patient values and wishes.
Discuss what CPR involves + likely outcomes.
Communicate to relevant team + family per patient wishes.

title: Breaking bad news consultation
consentNotes: Patient-centred; check what patient wants to know first.

steps.step: Find out what patient knows already (perception).
Explore what patient wants to know (invitation).
Give the information (knowledge) — warning shot first.

redFlags: Severe distress / suicide risk after news.

title: Vulnerable adult / domestic abuse screening
indications: Vulnerable adult presenting with unexplained injury.

relative: Patient with severely impaired capacity (advocate involvement).

consentNotes: Counsel on confidentiality limits.

steps.step: Separate patient from any accompanying person.
Refer to multi-agency risk assessment conference (MARAC) if high-risk.

title: Naloxone administration for opioid overdose
indications: Suspected opioid overdose with respiratory depression.

absolute: Confirmed non-opioid cause of decreased consciousness.
relative: Chronic opioid user (precipitate withdrawal — use careful titration).

consentNotes: Counsel post-recovery on substance misuse + take-home naloxone.

steps.step: Confirm opioid overdose by triad: decreased consciousness + bradypnoea + pinpoint pupils.
Administer naloxone 0.4 mg IM (or IV/IN) initially.
Consider naloxone infusion in long-acting opioids.
Refer for substance misuse + provide take-home naloxone.

complications.management: Repeat naloxone; infusion if long-acting opioid.

title: Paediatric IV fluid resuscitation
consentNotes: Time-critical; implied consent.

steps.step: Recognise shock features: tachycardia, prolonged CRT, decreased urine output.
Give 10 mL/kg bolus of isotonic crystalloid over 5-10 min (Hartmann's).
steps.detail: Cautious in resource-rich, FEAST guidance in resource-limited.

steps.step: Reassess: response to fluid (HR + CRT + BP).
Repeat boluses up to 40-60 mL/kg with reassessment.

steps.detail: Adrenaline first-line in paediatric septic shock.

title: Pre-operative anaesthetic assessment
consentNotes: Counsel on anaesthetic options, risks, post-op recovery.

steps.step: Obtain detailed history (cardiovascular, respiratory, allergies, prior anaesthetic).
Examine airway (Mallampati, mouth opening, neck mobility).
Calculate ASA score and predicted morbidity / mortality.
Order indicated investigations (ECG > 65, bloods, lung function).
Identify high-risk and refer to senior anaesthetist.

title: Simple tooth extraction
consentNotes: Counsel on pain, bleeding, dry socket, infection.

steps.step: Apply forceps + extract with controlled rotation + traction.

postProcedureCare: Avoid rinsing 24 h then warm saline.

title: Hand hygiene — clinical procedure
indications: After patient contact / body fluid exposure.
consentNotes: Standard.

steps.step: Use alcohol handrub for routine; soap + water for visibly soiled or C. difficile.
Cover all surfaces (palms, fingers, thumbs, nail folds, wrists) for 20-30 seconds.
Allow to dry before patient contact.

title: Infection control isolation precautions
indications: Patient with infectious disease (e.g. C. difficile, MRSA, COVID, TB).
consentNotes: Patient + family education.

steps.step: Choose isolation type: standard, contact, droplet, airborne.
Place in side room with appropriate signage.
Provide PPE for staff and visitors per type.
Educate staff + family + patient on hygiene + visiting.

title: Intercostal nerve block
consentNotes: Counsel on pneumothorax risk + LAST + transient numbness.

steps.step: Needle inserted at inferior border of rib + walk off inferior edge.

title: Medical adult / paediatric circumcision
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + risks (bleeding, infection, cosmesis, sexual function).

steps.step: Achieve haemostasis with diathermy or sutures.

title: Bartholin abscess marsupialisation or word catheter

absolute: Severe infection / sepsis requiring IV antibiotics first.

equipment: Word catheter or sutures for marsupialisation.
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + recurrence risk + scarring.

steps.step: Insert Word catheter (small balloon) for 4-6 weeks OR marsupialise edges with sutures.

title: Point-of-care rapid influenza / respiratory virus testing
consentNotes: Counsel on procedure + need for nasopharyngeal swab.

steps.step: Tilt head back + insert swab into nasopharynx.

title: Systemic anti-cancer therapy administration
consentNotes: Detailed consent for chemotherapy regimen + monitoring.

steps.step: Verify treatment plan + drug + dose + route + duration with two staff.
Verify patient identity + counts + organ function.
Premedicate with antiemetic + hydration as needed.
Document drug, dose, duration, any reaction.

complications.management: Stop + manage per vesicant protocol; plastic surgery.

title: Radiotherapy side-effect assessment + management
consentNotes: Counsel on expected vs unexpected side-effects.

steps.step: Common acute effects: skin toxicity, mucositis, dysphagia, fatigue.
Common late effects: fibrosis, lymphoedema, secondary cancer, infertility.
Manage skin: moisturisers, gentle washing, sun protection.
Manage mucositis: mouth care, analgesia, topical agents.
Refer to dietitian for nutrition support if needed.
